{{Short description|American computational mathematician}}

'''Sven Leyffer''' is an American computational mathematician specializing in [[nonlinear optimization]]. He is a Senior Computational Mathematician in the Laboratory for Applied Mathematics, Numerical Software, and Statistics at [[Argonne National Laboratory]]. 

==Education==
Leyffer received a Vordiplom in Pure and Applied Mathematics from the [[University of Hamburg]] in 1989.
Leyffer obtained his Ph.D. in 1994 from the [[University of Dundee]] under doctoral advisor [[Roger Fletcher (mathematician)|Roger Fletcher]].
His dissertation was ''Deterministic Methods in Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming''.{{r|dissertation}}

==Recognition==
In 2006, Leyffer was awarded, alongside Roger Fletcher and Philippe L. Toint, the Lagrange Prize from the Mathematical Programming Society (MPS) and the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] (SIAM).{{r|LP|LP1}}

In 2009, Leyffer was named a Fellow of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] (SIAM) for ''contributions to large-scale nonlinear optimization.''{{r|SF|SF1}}

==Service==

From 2017 to 2021, Leyffer was Editor-in-Chief of the journal [[Mathematical Programming]] B.{{r|MP}}

Leyffer is president (2023-2024) of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] (SIAM).{{r|SP|SP1}}
